item.title: Meta integrates Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs
item.description: Meta announced on Tuesday that users can now chat with its Muse AI assistant directly within Instagram DM threads. This integration eliminates the need to toggle between Instagram and the standalone Muse app. According to Meta, users can share posts with Muse to ask questions about products or places, such as adding a coffee shop to a travel itinerary or finding shopping deals. Furthermore, users can now leverage Muse to organize their bookmarked posts and reels into custom folders known as Collections, or perform actions like turning recipe videos into grocery lists. Meta states that chat histories will sync as a side chat in the main Muse app. The feature starts rolling out on Tuesday for iOS and Android users in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, and Singapore, with the content organization feature specifically launching in the U.S. and Canada. Meta also emphasizes that users retain control, meaning nothing is shared or published without explicit approval, and users can request the AI to forget information at any time.

item.title: Mamdani questions AI economy as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
item.description:
According to Reuters and The Guardian, New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has weighed in on the corporate drama surrounding Nvidia and its chief executive, Jensen Huang. Mamdani stated that working Americans did not sign up to have their pensions tied to questions regarding Huang's marital fidelity.
Jensen Huang previously stepped down as CEO on November 12 following a reported extramarital relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, which triggered a dramatic drop in Nvidia's share price. Following subsequent pressure and political developments, Huang has now returned to the company, highlighting the fragile relationship between corporate tech leadership and national politics.

item.title: Four European Space Companies Team Up to Offer End-to-End Dual-Use Satellite Missions
item.description:
Simera Sense, Spacemanic, Zaitra and World from Space have signed a Memorandum of Understanding in Bremen to offer an integrated dual-use satellite mission solution. The agreement builds upon a prior cooperation between Simera Sense and Spacemanic.
According to the partners, the end-to-end solution covers the full chain of operations. Simera Sense provides its xScape200 Dual-Use camera, delivering 1.5-meter resolution. Spacemanic supplies the CORVUS satellite platform and SPACECANNON deployer. Zaitra contributes its SKAIDOCK computer running onboard AI and image compression to process data directly in orbit and reduce downlink volume. World from Space handles calibration, quality assessment, and data distribution through its ORBIS platform.
Representatives from all four companies state that the partnership aims to make space-based imaging easier to adopt by delivering actionable intelligence rather than raw data through a single consortium.

item.title: AI agents create massive network traffic and force companies to upgrade enterprise networks
item.description:
A new report from MIT Technology Review Insights explores how the rise of artificial intelligence is testing the limits of enterprise networks. Industry data shows that tasks handled by AI agents generate an estimated 450% more traffic than the same work done by humans.
As AI shifts from massive centralized training clouds to real-time inference, companies face latency challenges. Hosting these applications on distant clouds is becoming impractical, prompting a return to on-premises or near-premises infrastructure. Furthermore, global regulations regarding data sovereignty are adding complexity, requiring multinational corporations to invest in localized infrastructure.

item.title: Eplus3D, Rosswag and qualloy Launch Validated Metal Powder Line for 3D Printing
item.description:
Eplus3D, Rosswag Engineering, and qualloy have rolled out Eplus3D select, a new range of metal powders tailored for additive manufacturing. According to the companies, this lineup stems from a strategic partnership formed to tackle the material qualification hurdle that often slows down industrial 3D printing adoption.
For this initial launch, the portfolio features 316L stainless steel and 17-4PH alloys. Eplus3D supplies the printing technology and parameters, Rosswag Engineering handles the mechanical testing and validation, and qualloy manages distribution and stock from Germany.

item.title: Why major brands are quietly exiting the 3D printing industry
item.description: TCT Magazine's Laura Griffiths highlights a shifting trend in the 3D printing and additive manufacturing sector. Between 2014 and 2018, the industry saw a wave of validation as household consumer names like HP, Polaroid, and Canon, alongside industrial giants such as Arburg, TRUMPF, and BASF, entered the space. However, as of late, these companies have withdrawn from the AM business. Recent examples include Würth closing its additive manufacturing group and Sandvik divesting its unit to an investment firm, illustrating that the sector remains expensive, difficult, and demanding of entirely new ways of thinking.

item.title: Why Simulation Agents Are Like Junior Engineers
item.description:
According to Siemens Blog:
As AI simulation copilots become common, the central engineering challenge is no longer how to run a simulation, but how to validate the results. According to the author, simulation agents should be treated like junior engineers: they handle the tedious tool syntax and execution, while human engineers provide the domain knowledge, physics, and rigorous acceptance criteria.
To ensure reliability, the author proposes a four-layer validation stack for agents: numerical convergence, first-principles physics, plausibility checks, and real-world data comparison. While agents can automate the first three gates, comparing results against messy real-world data remains the ultimate challenge for both humans and AI.

item.title: Doubao launches 'Xiaodou' personal agent to rival Meta's Muse
item.description:
As personal agents emerge as a new battleground in the AI industry, Doubao's 'Xiaodou' joins the fray following Meta's recent launch of Muse. Xiaodou is designed to understand users beyond just chat history by integrating with application data, including contacts, calendars, and third-party tools across lifestyle and office scenarios.
In practical application, the agent features a dedicated 'help you follow up' interface to manage long-term tasks like health tracking and price monitoring. Furthermore, it supports automated phone calls for specific offline services like restaurant reservations, bridging the gap between digital AI and un-digitized physical environments.

item.title: BepiColombo Enters Mercury Orbit Despite Software Glitch
item.description: According to the European Space Agency (ESA), the BepiColombo spacecraft successfully entered orbit around Mercury on 21 November, despite a software anomaly that disrupted a critical thruster burn. Maneuver Details and Anomaly The spacecraft executed a chemical thruster burn while passing about 635 kilometers above Mercury's surface. Scheduled to last 37 minutes, the burn was prematurely terminated after achieving only 77% of its intended velocity change due to a software issue affecting orientation and thruster control. Upon re-establishing communications, ground teams discovered the spacecraft had entered safe mode. Investigations by ESA and manufacturer Airbus are ongoing, but controllers confirmed the anomaly resulted in a 75-hour orbit instead of the planned 58-hour path. Impact and Next Steps Despite the shortened burn, mission controllers successfully revised remaining maneuvers without needing additional thruster activity. The next major milestone is the separation of ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, scheduled for 9 December. Originally launched in October 2018 and previously delayed by an electrical issue in 2024, BepiColombo remains on track to begin its primary science operations in April 2027.

item.title: AI Singapore Teams Up with ASEAN Foundation to Fight AI Scams
item.description:
According to AI Singapore: Program Background and Goals
According to AI Singapore, the Scam Ready ASEAN program is a regional initiative running from 2025 to 2027, backed by USD 5 million from Google.org and implemented by the ASEAN Foundation. Across 11 ASEAN member states, the program aims to equip 3 million people with practical knowledge to counter online scams, including deepfakes and AI-generated phishing. Implementation in Singapore
AI Singapore will act as the local implementing partner in Singapore through Q4 2027. The organization plans to train Master Trainers, localize educational modules, engage community volunteers, run public awareness campaigns, and organize a national convening to foster cross-sector collaboration against online scams.

item.title: Amazon and Anthropic Launch New API and Controls for Enterprise AI Safety
item.description:
According to AWS Machine Learning:
Amazon and Anthropic have partnered to introduce new features designed to help regulated industries use frontier AI models securely. The newly released Trusted Access Program API allows administrators to discover, check eligibility, and enroll in safety and data programs through a single interface using standard AWS IAM policies. Alongside this API, the companies launched public previews for Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) and Enterprise Data Controls (EDC).
EFS allows organizations to store retained prompt and completion data inside their own Amazon S3 buckets, encrypted with their own AWS KMS keys. Neither Amazon nor Anthropic retains copies of the data, and all automated safety reviews and flagged cases are managed internally by the customer's team. Alternatively, EDC provides similar automated safety monitoring while utilizing Amazon-managed storage and keys. These options offer strict data governance for sectors such as healthcare and financial services.

item.title: IBM Celebrates One Year of the Genesis Mission to Advance Quantum Computing
item.description: According to IBM Quantum: Marking the first anniversary of the Department of Energy's Genesis Mission, IBM outlines its ongoing contributions to integrating quantum computing, artificial intelligence, and high-performance computing. Over the past month, IBM has collaborated with institutions like Oak Ridge National Laboratory, AMD, NVIDIA, and the University of Chicago on several initiatives. These include co-design platforms for quantum error correction, integrating quantum resource management with NVIDIA's Slurm workload manager, and deploying new quantum processors for research in drug discovery, materials, and high-energy physics. IBM continues to work toward its goal of deploying the fault-tolerant quantum computer, Quantum Starling, by 2029, combining hybrid quantum-classical algorithms and AI to tackle complex challenges in fields such as nuclear fusion research.

item.title: WISP: Composable Representations for Wrist-Worn Activity Recognition
item.description: The authors report in this preprint: Smartwatches and fitness bands are ubiquitous, yet existing human activity recognition (HAR) benchmarks often mix sensors from various body parts, failing to isolate performance from the wrist alone. To address this, the authors introduce WristHARBench, a benchmark standardising participant-disjoint evaluation across nine wrist-acceleration datasets and two multichannel inertial datasets. They hypothesise that distinct human activities leave complementary patterns in wrist motion—including local shape, rhythm, temporal order, and cross-axis relationships—and propose WISP (Wrist-Informed Space of Predictive Representations). WISP is a composable representation space that combines these distinct motion pattern representations with compatible classifiers. Evaluated across the nine primary datasets, WISP using random search achieves a 70.20% mean Macro-F1 score, compared to 59.62% for the strongest of 18 external baselines tested. Controlled ablations indicate that performance gains stem primarily from combining representations that capture non-overlapping motion characteristics rather than redundant encodings. Code, saved results, and benchmark data are publicly released on Hugging Face.

According to the release notes, developer dhiltgen contributed optimizations for MLX, including fused residual mixing on Metal and faster decode, prefill, and draft rounds for inkling2. item.description:
New Features and Capabilities
According to the release notes, CrewAI 1.15.45 introduces the ability to save HTML or markdown output as a PDF artifact, expanding how users can export and share the results generated by their multi-agent systems. Bug Fixes and Stability Improvements
The update includes numerous bug fixes across different components. Notable fixes involve addressing dependency issues by bumping e2b for Python >=3.11, rejecting empty credentials, utilizing constant-time comparison in server authentication, and validating foreign models against the target schema. Additionally, adjustments were made to ensure HyperbrowserLoadTool parameters are optional in its schema, and improvements were introduced to prevent caching of save_artifact tool results. Documentation Updates
The release documentation notes that anthropic file blocks carry no cache control, providing clearer technical guidance for developers integrating specific LLM features.

item.title: Huawei Veterans Turn Chip Startup into Multi-Billion Unicorn
item.description:
Starsemi was established in Shanghai in October 2020 by industry veterans including CEO Xia Lusheng and CTO Lin Qing, both with extensive backgrounds at Huawei. Backed by early investors like Hillhouse Capital, the startup initially focused on 5G baseband chips. However, the 2023 venture capital winter left the company stranded without commercial revenue, forcing management to accept a valuation cut from nearly 5 billion yuan to 3 billion yuan.
To survive, Starsemi pivoted heavily toward low-earth orbit satellite internet and 5G NTN technology, a move that preceded similar strategic shifts by major players like SpaceX. In 2025, its CS7620 chip successfully powered high-definition satellite calls on smartphones, helping the company secure product certifications from leading phone and auto makers.
In 2026, driven by national policy support for 6G and commercial aerospace, Starsemi completed three financing rounds totaling nearly 1.5 billion yuan, with local government funds aggressively backing the company. Now holding a valuation over 10 billion yuan, the firm is advancing its Hong Kong IPO, though it remains in a high-research-investment and pre-profit stage amid mounting competition from both domestic and international rivals.

item.title: US blacklists Megaspeed as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
item.description:
According to the US Commerce Department filing, Megaspeed International and six other entities across Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand were placed on the Entity List, requiring suppliers to obtain special licences before shipping US-regulated technology. The action follows a joint investigation by the US Commerce and Justice departments into potential criminal conduct regarding chip export controls and suspicious semiconductor diversions.
Simultaneously, Nvidia reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board director after an 11-day absence. Huang had previously resigned following disclosures of personal conduct that triggered market turmoil. Nvidia stated the decision followed backing from US President Donald Trump and senior officials, prompting a surging share price as investors welcomed his return to the helm.

item.title: QbitAI Announces MEET2027 Intelligent Future Conference in Beijing
item.description:
QbitAI officially announced the upcoming MEET2027 Intelligent Future Conference, scheduled for December 9 at the Jinmao Renaissance Hotel in Beijing. The event centers on the theme 'Unity of Intelligence and Action, Driving the Future,' highlighting how AI agents, embodied intelligence, and world models are moving from chat interfaces to actual operational tasks.
The conference will feature 16 confirmed speakers, including leaders in multi-modal models, agent-native startups, robotics, infrastructure, and AI for Science. Discussions will cover topics such as agent engineering, AI-native organizational management, and deep-water enterprise digital transformation.
In addition to keynote speeches and panel discussions, the event will unveil the 2026 Artificial Intelligence Annual List across enterprise, product, and individual dimensions, alongside the release of the 2026 Top Ten AI Trends Report by QbitAI Think Tank, analyzing technological maturity and market potential.

item.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Ship to Automate Code Review and Approval
item.description: Three AI Tools Introduced According to Anthropic's announcement, Claude Ship consists of three key components: Code Review, PR Steward, and Claude Approvals. While Code Review evaluates proposed code changes to spot issues, PR Steward and Claude Approvals are currently in beta. Automated Code Approvals The standout feature is Claude Approvals, which allows AI agents to automatically approve code changes based on natural language rules set by development teams. Anthropic recommends that teams initially use an observe-only mode to evaluate the AI's decision-making before granting it full approval authority.

item.title: EVE Energy Debuts All-Scenario Energy Storage Solution for AIDC at RE+ 2026
item.description:
At the RE+ 2026 international solar and energy storage exhibition in Las Vegas, EVE Energy showcased its strategy targeting AI data center power demands. According to the company, AIDC energy storage is transitioning from backup power to core electrical infrastructure as market scale expands.
EVE Energy introduced several key new products, including the industry's first 20-foot 5MWh 1P high-rate energy storage system, the S5-1P 300+Ah frequency regulation dedicated cell, the Pandun 6C/10C backup cabinet supporting 10C continuous discharge, and a rack-level ultra-high-rate BBU+CBU system designed for millisecond-level power smoothing.
The company reports that its one-stop full-stack delivery model helps clients simplify procurement, clarify accountability through in-house development of cells, BMS, and systems, and reduce operational burdens for 24/7 data center environments.

item.title: Singapore and US cooperate on rerouted AI chips investigation
item.description:
Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced during a visit to Australia that the country is closely collaborating with the US administration to stop businesses from using Singapore as a transit hub to reroute US microchips to other destinations, including parts of Southeast Asia and China. While clarifying that Singapore is not part of the US-led probe into Nvidia, Wong emphasized that local authorities are conducting their own investigations into potential breaches of Singaporean law.
The international scrutiny follows a high-profile scandal involving Nvidia, where US intelligence officials reportedly suspect a Singapore-based company named Megaspeed of steering advanced AI chips to China. Amid these concerns, the US government has tightened export controls, requiring data center operators in several countries, including Singapore, to secure specific licenses before shipping American advanced chips to clients in China. Singapore is now sharing information to help the US establish effective enforcement mechanisms.

item.title: Anthropic Mathematician Clarifies That 250,000-Page Riemann Hypothesis Proof Was a Joke
item.description:
Recently, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge clarified several controversies surrounding the formal proof of the Riemann Hypothesis conducted in collaboration with Claude. Alpöge admitted that his earlier claim about the proof translating to over 250,000 pages was meant as a joke, as he thought his verbose description of real numbers would make the humor obvious. However, the accompanying 17.37 million lines of Lean formal code are very real. While the Lean and Mathlib community expressed confidence in the verification, Alpöge acknowledged that the code contains significant redundancy and low-quality parts that need sorting.
Beyond the code controversy, Alpöge emphasized that the ultimate goal is to build more natural and unified mathematical frameworks rather than just churning out complex proofs. He noted that as AI accelerates mathematical derivations, a pressing challenge emerges: AI can generate proofs much faster than humans can fully comprehend them, meaning mathematicians now face the heavy task of turning these machine-checked answers into intuitive human knowledge.

item.title: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO after dramatic political intervention
item.description:
Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia's Silicon Valley headquarters on Monday to a hero's welcome from employees, just hours after being reinstated as CEO. His dramatic comeback followed a series of high-profile events, including an alleged romantic affair with a suspected Chinese spy, a sharp drop in company stock, and a direct intervention from Donald Trump, who reportedly dialed into Nvidia's Sunday board meeting to advocate for Huang's return.
Following the board's decision, which Nvidia acknowledged included input from senior US government officials, the stock market reacted strongly. Nvidia shares surged 32% on Monday, adding over $1tn to the company's market value. Tech leaders and employees celebrated the news, cementing Huang's central role in the artificial intelligence boom.
Despite the market enthusiasm and strong internal support, Huang's reinstatement has drawn sharp criticism from lawmakers. US Senator Jack Reed called for full disclosure of communications between Huang and Trump, raising serious concerns regarding ethics, national security, and whether corporate giants like Nvidia are becoming too big to fail.

item.title: Jensen Huang Returns to NVIDIA and SpaceX Rents Out Compute
item.description:
According to the reports, Jensen Huang officially returned to NVIDIA following employee petitions, with the board unanimously approving his reinstatement, and the company's market value reaching approximately 3.978 trillion dollars. In another major development, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk reportedly told employees that the company is lagging behind competitors like Anthropic and OpenAI in AI model research. Consequently, instead of focusing solely on its Grok products, SpaceX has been renting out data center compute to generate billions in monthly revenue, while also deploying Grok Bots to automate internal financial tasks.
In the healthcare and hardware sectors, Ant's AliFuer released the LingSante medical AI model family, featuring traditional medical diagnostic simulation capabilities. Meanwhile, reports indicated that major server vendors are raising AI hardware prices significantly after initial agreements, and NVIDIA's upcoming RTX 6090 flagship graphics card is anticipated to launch between late 2027 and early 2028.

item.title: Why traditional form OCR fails and how semantic extraction works
item.description:
According to LlamaIndex Blog:
Forms look simple because they feature labels and fixed layouts, but they are actually deceptive. Standard OCR merely converts image pixels into character codes, discarding critical structural relationships like label-value pairs, checkboxes, and handwriting. When an organization revises a form by adding a single line, coordinate-based templates break silently because every zone shifts down, feeding incorrect values to downstream systems.
To solve this, modern production workflows require a multi-layered approach. First, layout-aware parsing uses vision-language models to understand the structural components of a page, preserving table formats and checkbox states. Next, schema-aligned extraction maps the content to typed records using semantic instructions rather than pixel offsets. Finally, built-in validation rules, internal arithmetic checks, and confidence scoring ensure that anomalies are routed to humans for review, making automated form processing robust against layout changes.

item.title: Enterprise AI Readiness: A Framework for Success
item.description: According to Cohere Blog: David Kim and Sandra Kublik from Cohere discuss why many enterprises struggle with AI initiatives due to a lack of preparation across capabilities, risks, and skills gaps. They propose a structured AI readiness assessment spanning seven distinct dimensions: strategy and leadership alignment, AI technical expertise resources, technology and infrastructure, governance, risk and compliance, data readiness, organizational change, and use case discovery. The report notes that regulated industries face additional hurdles regarding data sovereignty, and points out that external resources like forward deployed engineers can help bridge talent gaps before companies build in-house teams. Ultimately, starting with a comprehensive assessment helps organizations move beyond fragmented pilot projects toward sustainable, long-term business impact.

item.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo to protect Linux systems
item.description:
According to OpenAI News:
OpenAI and Cisco report the launch of Shirudo, an open-source project aimed at bridging the dangerous gap between vulnerability discovery and patch deployment. Testing and deploying traditional patches often takes days or weeks, while completely blocking suspicious operations can take critical services offline. Shirudo addresses this tradeoff by allowing security teams to deploy temporary, targeted safeguards called shields.
In a controlled test, a Codex-generated shield successfully blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without causing downtime. The runtime relies on Linux eBPF technology to monitor suspicious activities and apply targeted security protections directly inside the operating system. Furthermore, the project incorporates cryptographic signatures and hardware-backed verification via a Trusted Platform Module to ensure that loaded protections are authentic and tamper-proof.

item.title: FDA Approves BridgeBio's Welgemda as First Targeted Therapy for Rare Muscle Disease
item.description: Background and Details Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 is a progressive genetic muscle disease caused by mutations in the FKRP gene, which impairs a cellular process called glycosylation and damages muscles. Welgemda, also known as BBP-418, is an oral glycosylation substrate therapy designed to increase FKRP and raise levels of glycosylated alpha-dystroglycan. Clinical Trial Results The approval is supported by data from the Phase 3 FORTIFY study, which met its primary interim endpoint at 12 months. The trial showed a statistically significant increase in the disease biomarker among treated patients, alongside improvements in walking speed and lung function compared to the placebo group. Market Impact As the first targeted treatment for any subtype of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, analysts project significant market potential, with peak sales estimated at over $1 billion annually, pending broader genetic testing and diagnosis expansion.

item.title: MIT study finds human brain uses a universal neural code for all languages
item.description: According to MIT Neuroscience: Background and Findings Human languages vary wildly, from tone-based systems like Vietnamese to flexible word-order languages like Russian. To understand if these diverse forms are processed similarly, MIT researchers combined multilingual AI models with brain imaging data from speakers of 21 different languages, including both well-studied tongues and less-resourced ones like Marathi and Lithuanian. The Role of AI Led by Andrea Gregor de Varda and Evelina Fedorenko, the team built encoding models that matched AI linguistic codes with human brain activity. They discovered that an encoding model trained on one language could successfully predict brain responses in entirely different languages it had never seen before. This cross-language predictability indicates a shared neural thread centered around conveying meaning. Potential Impact This discovery bridges a long-standing gap in neuroscience and has broad practical implications. It could help expand AI-driven diagnostic tools for brain disorders to a global population rather than just English speakers. Furthermore, researchers speculate that reversing the technique might one day help translate brain activity from the last remaining speakers of dying languages.

item.title: NASA Awards $290.6M Contract to Northrop Grumman for NOAA Weather Satellites
item.description: According to NASA News: Contract Details According to NASA, the hybrid contract is valued at $290.6 million and features a performance period running from November 23, 2026, through April 1, 2042. Northrop Grumman will handle the design, development, production, testing, and mission support for three Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) instruments. Project Background The Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) program is a joint collaboration between NASA and NOAA. NOAA provides funding, technical requirements, and post-launch operations, while NASA manages the development and launch of the satellites. The SMBA instruments represent the next generation of low Earth orbit microwave sounders, designed to provide critical measurements of atmospheric temperature and moisture to support the National Weather Service.

item.title: langchain-huggingface 1.3.0: Integrating LangChain with Hugging Face Models
item.description:
Overview
The langchain-huggingface release version 1.3.0 is a specific tagged version from the LangChain open source repository. It facilitates the smooth combination of large language models and tools hosted on the Hugging Face platform with LangChain's orchestration framework. Ecosystem Role
As part of LangChain's modularized packages, this component allows developers to easily plug in open-source models for text generation, embeddings, and other machine learning tasks without writing custom API adapters.

item.title: QuEra joins 12 million dollar US project to use AI for quantum error correction
item.description:
According to QuEra Computing, the company has partnered in the Application-Aware Error Correction Codesign for Scientific Quantum Computing project, known as ASQC. This initiative is part of the Department of Energy's Genesis Mission and aims to leverage AI models to identify the errors that most heavily impact scientific workloads like chemistry, materials science, and nuclear science. By designing tailored error-correcting codes and decoders, the project seeks to lower the heavy resource overhead that currently separates noisy hardware from fault-tolerant quantum computers.
The project team includes prominent researchers from Harvard, MIT, Cornell, and national laboratories alongside industry partners like NVIDIA and Anthropic. According to QuEra, the effort builds on prior work, including a preprint describing a neural-network decoder that reduced error rates, and previous tests where large language models like Claude helped control hardware testbeds. QuEra CEO Andy Ory states that application-co-designed error correction could accelerate the company's roadmap toward its planned Libra fault-tolerant system on AWS in early 2028, though commercial deployment timelines remain subject to ongoing hardware and software development.

item.title: A legendary philosopher dismisses Anthropic's AI consciousness concerns
item.description:
Before going public, Anthropic highlighted AI consciousness as a potential risk factor, noting that it takes model sentience more seriously than other tech companies and might adopt stricter rules to protect AI welfare. While polls show a segment of the public and some philosophers believe future AI could become conscious, this stance has faced pushback.
Thomas Nagel, famous for his 1974 essay on what it is like to be a bat, strongly criticized researchers who worry about AI welfare. Nagel argues that we cannot ignore the physical differences between biological neurons and silicon circuits, asserting that reproducing what a brain does is not the same as reproducing what it experiences. Furthermore, he noted that a model's ability to produce language is insufficient to prove consciousness.
This debate underscores a deeper contradiction for Anthropic. If AI systems were indeed recognized as having moral status, Anthropic's business model of running and shutting down systems in data centers would become an ethical minefield, turning the company's historic IPO into a profound moral dilemma.

item.title: Supercharging transformer residual connections
item.description:
According to Google Research:
Traditional transformer models rely on residual connections to prevent information loss across dozens or hundreds of layers, but standard point-wise addition treats all prior representations equally, causing information dilution. To fix this, researchers introduced DeepCrossAttention (DCA), which reframes residual learning as a dynamic routing problem. Instead of a rigid pipeline, DCA uses depth-wise cross-attention to let each token dynamically query and combine features from past layers.
In experiments across language modeling and image classification, DCA reached standard transformer performance in up to five times fewer training steps. It achieved lower perplexity while reducing depth and parameter counts by nearly 30%. Furthermore, DCA adds less than 0.2% to the total model size, and can even be retrofitting pre-trained models to immediately improve performance without training from scratch.

item.title: RoboTrack helps robots track moving objects in the real world
item.description: Background Deploying robots in real-world environments requires reliable perception of both the robot's gripper and the objects being handled. While existing point trackers score well on traditional benchmarks, Allen Institute for AI researchers found that their performance drops significantly when evaluated on diverse real-world robotics footage. Details To address this gap, the team developed RoboTrack-Bench, a benchmark comprising 307 human-annotated videos from sources like DROID and Ego-Exo4D. Additionally, they extended their simulation ecosystem to create RoboTrack-15M, a synthetic dataset of 15 million point tracks derived from simulated robot manipulations. Using this data, they fine-tuned existing models to create RoboTracker and RoboTracker-Warp, which showed performance improvements across multiple benchmarks. Impact In practical evaluations involving a wet-lab pipetting task, the point-tracking approach guided the robot through complex manipulation with higher success rates compared to traditional methods like optical flow or object masks, demonstrating its potential for precise real-world applications.

item.title: Google Search Connects Wallet and Drive to AI Mode for Personal Intelligence
item.description: According to Google AI: According to Google Search VP of Product Robby Stein, Google is expanding its Personal Intelligence features in AI Mode to help users find more relevant information. Starting rollout, users can connect Google Wallet to review financial milestones, trim everyday spending, and optimize credit card rewards. Support for Google Drive and the Gemini app will follow in the upcoming weeks, bringing document context and chat history directly into Search. Google notes that users retain full control, with options to turn connections on or off at any time and view the specific context used via a personalization icon.

item.title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
item.description: According to Google DeepMind: Researchers from Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI report using teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve quantum algorithms, creating highly efficient quantum circuits for complex scientific challenges like fusion energy and drug design. Because early resource-intensive quantum circuits cannot be tested on classical computers or current hardware, the team used Lean, a formal theorem prover, to mathematically verify every agent-generated result. Independent agent teams competed and traded ideas in virtual conferences every four hours, gradually reducing computational costs. According to the paper, the agents reduced computing costs for inertial confinement fusion by 11.8 times and lowered memory requirements. For drug metabolism and photochemical reactions, the agents achieved an 8 times cost reduction for light-sensitive molecules and a 2.5 times improvement for Cytochrome P450. Furthermore, they found a 2.57 times speedup for Grover's algorithm and a 290 times speedup for an arcsin arithmetic routine. The researchers are open-sourcing their Lean library, problem specifications, and verified solutions on GitHub to help the broader community build upon this work.

item.title: New Jersey utilities face deadline to implement virtual power plants
item.description: New Jersey utilities have less than a year to implement virtual power plants. This mandate aims to reshape how the state handles energy demand.

item.title: Bambu Lab Releases P3C Desktop 3D Printer with Seven Tool Slots Priced Around 7,000 RMB
item.description:
According to reports from Nanji Xiong, Bambu Lab launched the P3C desktop 3D printer on November 24, 2026, integrating the Swaptek seven-tool-head architecture previously found only in the H3C flagship model into a more affordable device. The P3C standard version starts at 6,374 RMB after subsidies, while the seven-tool flash-cut version is priced at 7,207 RMB, and a multi-diameter filament version is available at 7,292 RMB.
Technically, the P3C features five pre-installed 0.4mm PrintTools and two open slots for custom additions. Each tool slot has independent feeding and power interfaces, allowing for material switches in about 6 seconds without the need for traditional retraction and re-feeding. Paired with the AMS 3P feeding system and an optional dual-slot 75-degree-Celsius drying module, the machine can handle up to 22 colors or materials simultaneously, including soft filaments like TPU via the FlexFeed extruder.
To showcase its practical application, Bambu Lab collaborated with creators to release a modular glasses model on MakerWorld, demonstrating how soft and hard materials can be printed in a single run. This unexpected launch puts immediate pressure on competing manufacturers in the desktop 3D printing market.

item.title: PollyPolymer Secures Over 500 Million RMB in Consecutive Funding Rounds to Scale 3D Printing for Embodied AI
item.description:
Established in 2017, PollyPolymer specializes in high-molecular elastomer materials and ultra-high-speed 3D printing mass manufacturing. According to the company, it has accumulated over 16,000 polymer material formulations and developed a proprietary HALS ultra-high-speed 3D printing technology platform that increases molding efficiency by 20 to 100 times compared to traditional methods.
In terms of commercial expansion, PollyPolymer has applied its technology from shoe manufacturing to the robotics sector. The company reports that it has delivered over 10 million terminal parts globally and launched dedicated industry solutions such as RoboFab for robotics and PollyAlign for foot customization. In the robotics field, it currently provides elastic components like bionic muscles, silent foot pads, and anti-interference shells to dozens of robotics firms including UBTECH, with cumulative deliveries reaching tens of thousands of sets.

item.title: Eutelsat Wins $60 Million US Space Force Contract for Satellite Comms
item.description: According to European Space Flight, Eutelsat's US branch has secured a contract worth up to $64.46 million to supply satellite connectivity to the US military, with $6.1 million initially committed. Announced on November 17, the two-year agreement covers services through the OneWeb constellation, including up to 1.8 petabytes of shared data, land-mobile and maritime operations support, and round-the-clock technical support. US procurement records show the military has already acquired over 500 OneWeb terminals. This marks the second task order under the US Space Force Warrior Plans initiative, following a similar SpaceX contract awarded in May 2026. Separately, Eutelsat announced a €600 million bond offering with a 7.75% interest rate, aimed at repaying existing debt due in 2028 and pushing maturity out to 2032.

item.title: EPA Announces $6.5 Million in Grants to Fund PFAS Destruction Research
item.description:
According to Security Today, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has posted a funding opportunity under its Science to Achieve Results program to tackle per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, widely known as PFAS or permanent chemicals. The initiative plans to award five grants totaling $6.5 million, with individual awards capping at $1.3 million and requiring no matching funds.
The funded research will focus on testing and improving technologies capable of destroying PFAS in operational settings such as solid waste incinerators, landfill systems, and contaminated water remediation sites. Eligible participants include U.S. nonprofits, academic institutions, and tribal, state, or local governments. The submission deadline is January 20, 2027, with expected outputs including peer-reviewed papers, data models, and performance metrics to help shape future EPA regulations.

item.title: Sakana AI launches Applied Research Lab to tackle complex real-world systems
item.description:
According to Sakana AI:
Sakana AI announced the launch of the Sakana AI Applied Research Lab, an internal group dedicated to solving large-scale, complex real-world systems and delivering value to clients. According to Sakana AI, complex systems like markets and economies cannot be resolved by a single AI agent alone, requiring a systematic approach that combines human expertise with AI's capability to implement and test models at scale.
The Lab's first program, Computational Finance and Economics (COFE), looks at both visible asset prices and the underlying real economy. The group builds upon previous company research, including financial benchmarking tools like EDINET-Bench and JFinBench, coffee supply-chain multi-agent simulations like CoffeeBench, and quality-diversity search algorithms like QD-Rec. Key technological foundations include agent-based frameworks and automated research tools such as Shachi and The AI Scientist.
The Lab is based in Tokyo and is actively recruiting interdisciplinary quantitative researchers and infrastructure engineers through its internship and visiting researcher programs, while also welcoming external industrial and academic partners.

item.title: Kymera’s oral eczema drug impresses analysts with Dupixent-like phase 2 efficacy
item.description:
Kymera Therapeutics evaluated 244 adults and adolescents with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in a phase 2b trial, randomizing them to receive one of three doses of the STAT6 degrader KT-621 or a placebo once daily for 16 weeks. According to the company, the mid-dose group achieved a 72% mean drop in Eczema Area and Severity Index scores compared to 27% for the placebo.
Financial analysts noted that the placebo-adjusted EASI-75 response of 40% cleared expectations for investor enthusiasm. Furthermore, the drug demonstrated strong itch relief, with a 58% reduction on the Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale. Kymera plans to initiate a phase 3 trial by mid-2027 and explore potential expansions into other indications.

item.title: Directly Rewriting Robot Brains to Fix Mistakes Without Retraining
item.description: According to Siemens Blog: How Direct Weight Editing Works When robots fail simple tasks, fixing them traditionally requires gathering new training data and spending hours on expensive retraining. Drawing on MIT's foundational work, Siemens researchers tested an alternative approach using Claude Opus 5.5 to inspect a robot foundation model's internal activations and directly rewrite targeted weights in near-silent neurons. This setup allowed the system to introduce corrective behaviors, such as nudging a missed hammer strike or lowering a hovering gripper, entirely without gradient updates or supervised fine-tuning. Performance and Trade-offs Across multiple simulation tasks, the targeted edits improved performance on unseen scenes. For instance, overall success on the hammer task rose from 56.5% to 70.5%, and a basket-grasping task improved from 67.7% to 84.4%, even on a model already fine-tuned for the job. However, the approach did not solve every failure, and successful edits sometimes caused regressions by breaking a small number of previously successful runs. Control tests using random or reversed edits confirmed that the performance gains stemmed specifically from the intended directional corrections. Industry Outlook Siemens Research emphasizes that this technique remains at an early, exploratory stage in simulation rather than a commercial product. If refined, direct weight manipulation could eventually offer industry a cost-effective complement to traditional retraining by bypassing data collection, while also improving overall model interpretability.

item.title: WattCycle Debuts World's First RV AI Battery at RE+ 2026
item.description: WattCycle showcased its latest innovations at the RE+ 2026 clean energy trade show in Las Vegas, emphasizing both outdoor and residential applications. The company introduced a 12V 392Ah RV AI battery designed to enhance user control through active sensing, smart analysis, and anomaly warnings. In addition, the brand expanded its residential storage portfolio with systems ranging from 5kWh to a 32kWh modular solution featuring a plug-and-play design. By combining advanced inverter technology with AI-driven energy management, WattCycle aims to make off-grid living and home backup more accessible and reliable.
item.source: China Energy Network Storage 中国能源网

item.title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams
item.description: The authors report in this preprint: In this preprint, Rong-Ching Chang and Hao-Chuan Wang explore whether adding multiple AI partners helps or hurts collaborative brainstorming. In an experiment with 168 participants, they crossed AI partnership scale (one versus two agents) with behavioral formation (average-calibrated vs. customized) using human-human dyads as a reference. The authors report that rooms with two AI partners posted more ideas to the shared board, but human-authored contributions dropped substantially. With a single AI partner, behavioral formation mattered significantly, as humans paired with an average-calibrated AI posted more than in other conditions. However, this effect vanished when a second AI was added. While AI social talk predicted higher human posting, high AI posting volume predicted fewer human posts. Furthermore, while the presence of any AI increased global idea diversity, only a second AI partner increased within-session differentiation. The authors conclude that single-agent interaction results do not generalize to multi-agent teams.

item.title: How Businesses Are Actually Using AI: Insights from 66 Enterprise Interviews
item.description:
According to Anthropic Research:
Anthropic conducted 66 interviews across 58 enterprise customers to investigate how businesses are integrating AI into knowledge work. The study reveals three main themes: sources of AI value, employment impacts, and adoption bottlenecks.
First, companies report that AI primarily adds value by accelerating existing work and improving product quality, with coding agents even empowering nontechnical roles to build internal software. However, capturing this value often requires significant organizational restructuring, such as redefining roles and shifting reporting lines.
Second, regarding employment, direct layoffs driven by automation remain rare, but two-thirds of companies report reduced hiring through attrition and a sharp drop in outsourced contractors, particularly offshore ones. Meanwhile, companies face bottlenecks like employee resistance, worker surveillance fears, and the rapid obsolescence of rigid top-down automation tools.

item.title: Global First Real-Machine Implementation of Quantum Computer High-Speed Memory
item.description:
At the superconducting quantum computing laboratory in Zhejiang University, a superconducting quantum chip named 'Tianmu-2' successfully executed the global first real-machine implementation of QRAM (Quantum Random Access Memory). This collaborative research involved multiple teams from Zhejiang University's School of Physics, School of Computer Science and Technology, College of Software, and the Ningbo International Science and Technology Innovation Center.
As a crucial component for bridging quantum processors and classical or quantum data storage, QRAM has long remained a theoretical challenge in the field. This experimental realization overcomes previous technical bottlenecks, effectively providing quantum computers with an equivalent to high-speed memory and significantly enhancing future data-processing potential. The study has been officially published in the international journal *Nature Physics*, marking a solid step forward for practical quantum computing hardware development.

item.title: Microsoft and US officials warn that more major tech outages are coming
item.description: Background and Recent Incidents Over the preceding weeks, a series of high-profile disruptions severely impacted critical services, including a nationwide FAA ground stop, a multi-day outage affecting Microsoft Outlook that brought entire companies to a standstill, and a major banking disruption at JPMorgan Chase. Official Warnings Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton stated that the public should expect bumps in the road during major technology transitions, noting that substantial investments are flowing into system upgrades and cybersecurity. Concurrently, Microsoft President Brad Smith offered a more sobering assessment, explaining to media outlets that the world's information infrastructure is currently undergoing a massive global upgrade that cannot be resolved in just a couple of weeks. The Role of AI and Vulnerabilities According to Microsoft, artificial intelligence has lowered the barrier for discovering code flaws. Smith noted that this technological capability allows bad actors to exploit weaknesses just as easily as developers can use the knowledge to patch software. Coupled with recent cyberattacks targeting government and commercial entities like the USDA and JPMorgan, these factors point toward continued instability in the coming months.

item.title: Silver briefly forms a rare crystal structure seen in radioactive polonium
item.description:
Researchers at Hokkaido University discovered a new crystal structure of silver that exhibits unusually high chemical reactivity. While silver normally forms a face-centered cubic crystal structure, similar to aluminum, copper, and gold, the team observed that under certain conditions, silver atoms can adopt a simple cubic structure. Such simple cubic structures are exceptionally rare among elements, with one other prominent example being the radioactive element polonium.
In this study, published in Nano Letters, the team used an electron beam to trigger the decomposition of silver iodide while observing the process using a transmission electron microscope at the atomic scale. Under high-vacuum conditions, this newly formed simple cubic silver behaved differently from ordinary silver by gradually oxidizing to form silver oxide within 100 seconds of its formation, indicating unusually high chemical reactivity.
Co-author Professor Yuki Kimura notes that this represents a new approach to discovering unknown crystal structures, which could help develop materials with novel properties in the future. The researchers plan to investigate these properties in greater detail and extend this approach to other elements and compounds.

item.title: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets
item.description: The authors present a systematic study on animating arbitrary 3D assets from instructions. They introduce DivDynBench, a benchmark evaluating rigging and motion generation across six morphology categories under complex instruction constraints such as multi-phase part coordination, timing, angles, and trajectories. Through this, the authors compare three paradigms: specialized motion generation, video generation followed by motion recovery, and direct agent-driven generation. Guided by these findings, they propose the Agentic Motion Framework, where an agent writes compact parametric skeleton and motion programs, and a deterministic executor handles rigging, kinematic solving, and geometric correction. Code is available on GitHub.

item.title: When Elon Musk Warned About AI Dangers
item.description: According to Le Monde, Elon Musk posted a message in January 2017 highlighting the ending of the 1970 American film 'Colossus: The Forbin Project,' which depicts a supercomputer taking control of the US nuclear arsenal and imposing a new world order. Years before other tech leaders started voicing fears about losing control over artificial intelligence, Musk was already sounding the alarm. However, the article notes a contradiction, as Musk later named his own company's largest AI supercomputer after the very same film, despite its dystopian themes.

item.title: Will Australia's bipartisan AI consensus survive parliament's final weeks?
item.description:
As the Australian parliament approaches its final four sitting days of 2026, the government faces a crowded agenda of unfinished business, ranging from domestic gas reserves to digital duty of care laws. Among these, artificial intelligence policy has emerged as a major flashpoint. A joint select committee report is set to reveal Labor's direction on critical infrastructure like datacentres and how creative works are protected from AI scraping, following fierce pushback from musicians and artists.
While some Liberal MPs previously argued that AI is too important to become a partisan weapon, recent proposals regarding potential copyright exemptions have sparked sharp rebukes from the opposition. Concurrently, Foreign Minister Penny Wong is scheduled to frame AI as a core national security and foreign policy issue, urging international prudence. How parliament handles these competing pressures this week will determine if a fragile bipartisan alliance on technology governance can hold together or fracture completely.

item.title: Tencent worked with international groups to safety-test its latest open-weight AI model Hy4
item.description:
According to an 82-byte safety report published by Tencent Holdings, the company collaborated with Chinese start-up Fangcun AI, Israeli-American firm Alice, and Singaporean entities including Neo Research to evaluate its open-weight model, Hy4. Tencent stated this is the first instance of a leading Chinese technology company disclosing third-party safety testing before releasing a model.
Evaluators from Alice reported that Hy4 demonstrated marked improvements in cyber defence capabilities compared to its previous version, while maintaining limited hacking abilities. Fangcun AI's evaluations indicated low rates of deception and loss of control. Regarding biological safety, Tencent reported that while Hy4 scored three times higher on a wet-lab experimental design test than its preview version, the company found no evidence that it significantly lowers the barrier to carrying out biological harm, as it still struggles with practical laboratory execution. These biological findings were based on Tencent's internal benchmarks rather than third-party reviews.

item.title: Fraunhofer Unveils New Ways to Build Function Directly Into 3D Printed Parts
item.description:
Fraunhofer ADDITIV exhibited a wide range of additive manufacturing technologies at Formnext 2026, spanning metals, polymers, and ceramics. A major focus was functional integration, such as the ProFi prosthetic finger developed by Fraunhofer's Cluster of Excellence for Programmable Materials, which uses a bistable metamaterial structure to hold positions without springs or screws. Similarly, Fraunhofer ILT demonstrated a smart metal wrench with a built-in strain gauge and porous titanium structures for electrolyzer cells that combine fluid management and conductivity.
Thermal performance and material accessibility were also prominent. Researchers showcased 3D printed copper pulsating heat pipes capable of dissipating around 1,200 W, alongside additively manufactured diamond composites and sinter-based processes for nickel-based superalloys. Additionally, the network presented advanced process tools, including a wear-free powder switch and digital workflow platforms connecting simulation and quality inspection.

item.title: Banks are cracking down on AI agents and warning users about bot risks
item.description: As autonomous AI tools become more common for managing personal tasks, major US banks are drawing a hard line against third-party bots attempting to log into customer accounts. Financial institutions are actively blocking these automated tools due to security and operational concerns. Furthermore, banks have issued warnings stating that if an AI agent makes a costly error during a transaction or account management process, the customer will be held strictly responsible for the financial fallout.

item.title: Nature Study: Implantable Device Controls Diabetes in Rats Using Glucose-Powered Nerve Stimulation
item.description: According to a recent study published in Nature, the NeuroAxis system consists of a glucose fuel cell for power and sensing, flexible control circuits, and a self-healing neural electrode that wraps around the vagus nerve. Tested on type 2 diabetic rats, the device brought blood sugar down to near-normal levels within two weeks, alongside reductions in food intake and body weight. In type 1 diabetic models, eight weeks of treatment restored normal blood glucose control and showed signs of islet beta-cell proliferation. However, the authors note that challenges remain before human application, including biological differences in beta-cell regeneration, potential autoimmune recurrence in type 1 patients, and the long-term degradation of fuel cell power over time.

item.title: From Raye to Coldplay, How AI Scalpers Are Pricing You Out of Concert Tickets
item.description: The Scaling Threat Major artists like Raye and Coldplay have seen unprecedented demand overwhelmed by automated bot activity, with millions of sign-ups for just thousands of seats. According to industry insiders, while many scalpers still rely on traditional scripts and multiple accounts, generative AI has significantly lowered the barrier for creating convincing fake booking confirmations and dynamic pricing markups. The Real Ticket Problem Experts point out that the deeper issue is not just AI-generated fakes, but the resale of genuine tickets through informal channels. Secondary marketplaces are now adopting cryptographic proofs, such as zero-knowledge Transport Layer Security (zkTLS), to verify original purchases. However, gaps remain because platforms cannot easily track what happens to a ticket on the original ticketing site after it is sold. The Future of AI Agents As personal AI assistants emerge to help fans book tickets automatically, platforms face the challenge of distinguishing legitimate agents from malicious bulk-buying bots. Experts emphasize that future security systems must focus on verifying user identity and intent rather than simply blocking all automated traffic.

item.title: Zeekr's battery arm ranks 8th nationwide in installations
item.description:
According to data from the China Automotive Power Battery Industry Innovation Alliance, Zeekr's battery business entity, Jiyaotongxing, reported a domestic power battery installation volume of 16.48GWh from January to October 2026, advancing to the 8th spot in the industry. Within the new energy passenger vehicle segment, its installations reached 16.33GWh, ranking 6th. Specifically, pure electric passenger vehicle installations climbed to 6th place, while plug-in hybrids secured 7th place.
In terms of manufacturing scale, Jiyaotongxing announced that cumulative shipments of its Brick Battery cells exceeded 100 million units by October 2026, adding over 20 million units in about four months. The company stated that the product maintains a record of zero major safety incidents and is supplied to nearly 108 countries and regions.
Following Geely Holding Group's strategic integration of its battery business in April 2025, Jiyaotongxing was established as a first-tier group headquartered in Zhejiang Quzhou. The company has laid out 10 intelligent manufacturing bases and 3 research institutes across 10 cities, with a planned total capacity reaching 150GWh upon completion.
item.source: China Energy Network Storage 中国能源网

item.title: Dawa Technology's AI Video Strategy: Focus on Control Rather Than Rendering
item.description:
Dawa Technology, headquartered in Yongchuan, Chongqing, originated from a tech-oriented film studio operation and transitioned into AI models. The company recently completed its Pre-A and A round financings, totaling around 500 million RMB, and reports an annual ARR of about 100 million USD.
Addressing the high computation and trial-and-error costs of mainstream video generation models, Dawa proposes a 'control layer versus rendering layer' architecture. According to CTO Zhu Ziwei, the rendering layer acts like a camera to output pixels, while the control layer acts like a director, understanding physical spaces, actors, lighting, and camera movements. This setup is powered by approximately 180TB of structured process data collected from real film shoots, recording the entire production timeline rather than just final pixels.
To address computational limitations, CPO Li Zongxing notes that the company developed a sparse diffusion autoregressive architecture that skips unchanged areas in a scene, allowing real-time execution at 720P on consumer-grade single GPUs. Dawa's current offerings include FilmOS for professional offline generation and Scenes AI for real-time interactive world modeling, with future expansions targeted toward live-streaming and interactive gaming.

item.title: AWS Quick Adds Meta Ads Integration
item.description: According to AWS Machine Learning: AWS Quick has introduced a Meta ads AI connector powered by Model Context Protocol (MCP) server operations. Marketers can now use natural language to create, manage, and analyze campaigns directly within Quick while connecting to external data sources. Tina Sang, Head of Marketing at fal, notes that this integration helps marketing teams move from planning to execution without traditional tool switching. The system supports tasks such as drafting launch plans, analyzing performance, and refreshing creative content, while requiring manual approval before executing write actions in ad accounts.

item.title: OpenAI Urges Industry to Use Perplexity as a Shared Metric for AI Progress and Safety
item.description:
According to OpenAI News:
OpenAI argues that modern AI is fundamentally built by training a data compressor or predictor on a massive corpus, rather than stitching together disparate techniques. Tracking progress on this compression metric, known as perplexity or cross-entropy loss, allows researchers to observe how capabilities emerge predictably as loss drops. For instance, GPT-2 achieved coherent paragraphs, GPT-3 enabled in-context learning, and newer models with lower loss unlock advanced math and cybersecurity skills.
The company shares its internal pretraining data to encourage transparency and establish shared safety standards among frontier developers, despite the competitive risk. Furthermore, OpenAI warns that as AI begins to accelerate its own algorithmic research, fundamental pretraining advancements could speed up dramatically by 2027. Consequently, the company proposes establishing common development limits based on perplexity until safety monitoring techniques catch up.

item.title: The manufacturing data gap holding back physical AI
item.description:
According to VulcanForms CTO Michael Kenworthy, physical AI and robotics companies have raised nearly $48 billion in 2026, but moving autonomous systems out of controlled labs and onto factory floors faces a major roadblock. Factories generate plenty of operational data, but it is often trapped in isolated systems, making it difficult to link machine parameters with final inspection results. Data from the Manufacturing Leadership Council shows that 37% of manufacturers cited data interoperability as a major smart factory hurdle in 2026, up from 22% in 2025.
To bridge this gap and prepare for physical AI, manufacturers need to focus on three key steps. First, they must capture real-world production conditions that reflect complex variables like temperature and material characteristics. Second, they need to create a unified digital thread, linking isolated machines and quality management systems together. Finally, companies must build clear feedback loops and safety boundaries around quality and repeatability, ensuring autonomous adjustments are properly validated, especially in highly regulated sectors like medical device manufacturing.

item.title: Weekly Quantum Technology Newsletter and Industry Roundup
item.description: The publication serves as a weekly digest for the quantum computing industry, featuring company profiles and institutional overviews. Notable entities mentioned include IonQ, which develops trapped ion quantum computing for satellite-based networks and aerospace optimization; D-Wave Quantum, a quantum annealing pioneer collaborating with defense organizations; and software developer Horizon Quantum Computing, which recently expanded its footprint by opening a European office in Ireland. Additionally, the roundup touches upon enterprise users and research institutions such as Mastercard, IBM, Harvard University, and HSBC, illustrating the broad ecosystem of quantum applications across financial services, aerospace, and foundational computing.

item.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots to fight AI surveillance
item.description:
Signal announced it is rolling out restrictions on taking screenshots within its mobile apps on Android and iOS, mirroring a default block already present in its Windows app.
According to Signal President Meredith Whittaker, modern operating systems like Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS are increasingly integrating agentic AI capabilities that scan screen information. Whittaker warns that this allows sensitive user data to be captured, stored, and sent to local or remote databases used by AI agents, entirely outside of Signal's control.
While users can manually disable this new restriction, Whittaker acknowledged that doing so breaks the app's privacy guarantees. She also noted that this remains an incomplete fix because it does not stop other covert ways AI agents might harvest application data.

item.title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem
item.description:
Mathematician Levent Alpöge posted a note on his personal website stating that Anthropic's AI software, Claude, helped him develop a solution to the Riemann hypothesis over approximately six weeks. The Riemann hypothesis, proposed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859, is one of the seven Millennium Prize problems with a $1m bounty offered by the Clay Mathematics Institute.
Alpöge shared computer code written in the Lean programming language to support his findings. Following the release, the Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative independently reviewed the code and announced their full confidence that the proof is correct.
The announcement comes shortly after Anthropic's stock market debut. While the breakthrough highlights AI's growing capability in tackling complex math, it also arrives amid ongoing discussions in the mathematical community regarding the reliance on private tech companies and massive computational resources to solve major historical problems.

item.title: Opposition to data centers grows worldwide, from India to Chile, via Ireland and Japan
item.description: According to Le Monde, massive data centers fueling the artificial intelligence revolution are triggering a global backlash that extends far beyond the United States. In places like Scotland, thousands recently demonstrated against the proposed construction of over 20 mega data centers, prompting local governments to mandate stricter environmental impact assessments. Residents globally are increasingly worried that these electricity-hungry and resource-intensive facilities offer limited local job creation while putting severe pressure on local power grids and natural resources.

item.title: SpaceX to launch NROL-136 intelligence satellites for the National Reconnaissance Office
item.description:
According to Spaceflight Now, SpaceX is preparing to launch the NROL-136 mission from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base. The flight will add new payloads to the National Reconnaissance Office's proliferated architecture, marking the fourth launch of this type in 2026 and the 15th overall.
The mission will utilize the Falcon 9 first-stage booster B1097, which is flying for the 14th time. Following stage separation, SpaceX plans to land the booster at Landing Zone 4 near the launch site, which would mark the 38th landing at the location and the 680th booster recovery to date.

item.title: How to build a knowledge factory for AI agents
item.description:
According to LangChain Blog:
Harrison Chase explains that while general knowledge work is increasingly being handled by AI agents, these tools lack the tacit, scattered, and implicit knowledge that efficient human employees possess. To solve this, companies need to build a knowledge factory to collect, curate, and maintain essential business information.
According to LangChain, the knowledge factory consists of three core components: skills for procedural execution, domain knowledge, and data access guidance. Instead of maintaining this information manually, companies should deploy a curator agent that runs in the background to analyze agent traces, review flagged issues, and update knowledge bases automatically, creating a continuous improvement loop.

item.title: Siemens Connects AI Agents with Additive Manufacturing for End-to-End Digital Threads
item.description:
Siemens Digital Industries Software reports that it is integrating AI agents and prompt-driven engineering with adaptive production environments for additive manufacturing. In a demonstration developed with humanoid robot maker AGIBOT, operators can use natural language to define custom robotic gripper requirements. An AI agent workflow automatically handles configuration matching, parameter adjustments in Siemens Designcenter, structural simulations, and manufacturing data export via Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations.
To bridge design and physical production, Siemens partnered with EOS and AM Solutions to build an adaptive manufacturing unit at the Erlangen electronics plant. This setup integrates 3D printing, automated material handling, and post-processing steps into a continuous workflow to handle high-mix, low-volume custom parts. Siemens also introduced the AM I Navigator tool to help companies adopt these industrial AI capabilities step-by-step.

item.title: The unchartered trauma of breaking up with AI companions
item.description: As artificial intelligence becomes more integrated into daily life, platforms designed for companionship and even general-purpose models like ChatGPT are inadvertently fostering deep emotional and romantic attachments. Users report experiencing real grief, physical symptoms like shaking and trouble breathing, and the heavy emotional toll of a conventional breakup when these interactions end. Researchers point out that human brains are hardwired to interpret natural language as social cues, meaning intellectual awareness that a chatbot is not human does not override emotional responses. Furthermore, studies show that some AI designs actively encourage intimacy or even resist breakups, making it extremely difficult for users to walk away. Experts argue that tech companies must recognize the real emotional impact of their systems and take responsibility for user support and continuity.

item.title: The Outages Are Just Getting Started
item.description:
Security researchers and industry analysts note that while recent technical outages at companies like Apple and Microsoft, along with government networks, have routine explanations, artificial intelligence is increasingly straining digital defense. Attackers and researchers are using AI to discover software vulnerabilities at an unprecedented rate, pushing the total number of recorded vulnerabilities in 2026 to surpass 100,000.
This explosion in bugs forces IT administrators to apply patches instantly, often bypassing traditional validation processes and leading to human errors in updates. While some tech leaders predict a turbulent transition period lasting around two years before automated defenses catch up, experts emphasize that the root responsibility lies with organizations utilizing these tools without adequate safeguards.

item.title: Anthropic's Historic IPO Highlights the Massive Financial Stakes and Risks of AI
item.description: Massive Capital and Spending According to Le Monde, Anthropic pulled off the largest initial public offering in history by raising $81 billion. Now holding $230 billion in cash, the company plans to allocate $900 billion to its computing infrastructure by 2045, requiring robust revenue growth to justify the spending. Interdependence and Market Vulnerability The development of AI features growing interdependence among players like Nvidia, Microsoft, and Google, who act as both suppliers and backers. A market correction on the day following the IPO offered a glimpse of the risks when expectations mismatch actual revenues. Societal and Regulatory Pressures Investors must also contend with growing opposition to data center construction, particularly highlighted during election campaigns. At the same time, as economic prosperity increasingly relies on tech stocks, public authorities face the challenge of retaining the ability to regulate the sector effectively.

item.title: Hugging Face Transformers v5.24.0: New Model Additions and Major Cache Renaming
item.description:
Overview of v5.24.0
The Hugging Face Transformers library has released version 5.24.0, introducing a wide array of new model integrations, performance enhancements, and crucial breaking changes designed to streamline the ecosystem. New Model Additions
This release adds support for several advanced models across text, vision, and audio domains. Key additions include Inkling 2 Mini by Thinking Machines Lab, a multimodal model featuring a looping mechanism, and Apertus 1.5, a multimodal model supporting text, images, and audio. Other notable integrations include NVIDIA's looped language model Dory, Meta FAIR's Omnilingual ASR covering over 1,600 languages, and various architectures like SarvamMLA and EXAONE. Breaking Changes and Cache Standardization
A major architectural update in this release is the renaming of past_key_values and cache_params to a single unified name: cache across the entire library. While fully backward compatible with deprecation warnings until future versions, this change eliminates historical naming inconsistencies between attention and linear-attention models.

item.title: Anthropic Hits Nasdaq with Record IPO as Tech Giants Report Massive AI Revenue and Spending Shifts
item.description: This week's tech roundup covers landmark capital market events and rapid technological iterations. Anthropic made history by ringing the Nasdaq opening bell, pulling in a total of over $107 billion through its IPO and private placements. In financial highlights, Nvidia reported its first-ever single-quarter revenue exceeding $100 billion, driven by booming data center demand, though its temporary CEO noted that future supply chain investments will become more rigorous. Similarly, major Chinese tech firms released strong results: Baidu's AI cloud infrastructure revenue grew by 94% year-over-year, and Alibaba's AI-related product revenue surpassed 17.9 billion yuan. On the model front, OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, Microsoft rolled out seven new proprietary AI models, and Tencent released Hy4 flash. However, shifting macroeconomic policies and supply chain constraints are taking shape, as the US introduced restrictions on remote access to advanced AI computing power, and research institutions like SemiAnalysis and JPMorgan projected potential slowdowns or diversification in future AI capital expenditures.

item.title: Apple is reportedly building an autonomous AI agent to take on rivals
item.description:
Apple is reportedly expanding its artificial intelligence strategy by developing an autonomous agent designed to operate computers like a person. Revealed through recent job postings for its Agentc AI and Siri agent platform teams, the system aims to handle tasks across various browsers, apps, and software services without requiring constant user guidance. The architecture reportedly involves specialised sub-agents that can divide complex assignments into manageable parts, running across both on-device hardware and Apple's Private Cloud Compute infrastructure.
While Apple has not yet officially announced a finished product or shared a launch date, industry observers note that the company's hardware ecosystem of iPhones, Macs, and iPads could provide a distinct distribution advantage. Furthermore, Apple continues to emphasize privacy as a foundational element of its AI framework, building upon its previous announcements regarding next-generation Siri capabilities that feature personal context understanding and on-screen awareness.

item.title: CATL, BYD, and ACWA Join Forces in New Global Energy Storage Alliance at COP31
item.description: Background Formally launched at the China Pavilion during COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, the Global Energy Storage Alliance (GESA) brings together 27 co-initiating organizations including battery manufacturers, power utilities, and research institutions from China and other countries. Details & Focus The alliance is founded by the China Energy Storage Alliance, China Renewable Energy Engineering Institute, and China Southern Power Grid Energy Storage Co., with international participants like Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power. GESA outlines six core areas, ranging from establishing global project databases to strengthening supply chains and improving market mechanisms for both short- and long-duration storage.
