Impact The initiative directly supports the global goal of tripling renewable capacity by 2030 by de-risking financing for emerging economies in regions like Southeast Asia and Latin America, marking a shift for China from exporting products to shaping global standards.

item.title: Fraunhofer IAPT uses ultrasound to remove 3D metal printing supports
item.description: Background and Process Removing support structures is traditionally one of the most labor-intensive and hazardous steps in metal additive manufacturing, often exposing workers to fine metal powder. To tackle this, Fraunhofer IAPT has created an ultrasonic process that applies high-frequency mechanical vibrations to printed components. By pairing custom-designed support structures with tailored vibration settings, the method concentrates stress where the supports attach, causing them to break away cleanly within a few minutes. Application and Industry Impact Originating from the Sonodent research project, the technology is initially being applied in dental technology but is designed to scale across other industries. While Fraunhofer IAPT focuses on ultrasonic vibrations, other players are tackling the same bottleneck through robotics, such as Rivelin Robotics, or redesigned breakaway structures, like those from SnowX, highlighting a broader industry push toward automated post-processing.

item.title: Sorbonne and Qubit Pharmaceuticals introduce VULCAN framework for efficient quantum chemistry
item.description:
According to a preprint on arXiv, researchers from Sorbonne Université and Qubit Pharmaceuticals developed VULCAN (Variational Upbuilding, Layered Compression, Adaptive N-body perturbation) to solve the major measurement bottleneck in traditional adaptive quantum algorithms. Instead of checking thousands of candidate operators one by one at every step, VULCAN derives relevant excitations quickly and appends full layers simultaneously.
In GPU-accelerated tests up to 32 qubits, the authors report that VULCAN achieved chemical accuracy using only 5% to 20% of the measurements required by standard batched methods across various molecules. The team also conducted an initial hardware validation on a Quantinuum trapped-ion processor for molecular hydrogen, successfully measuring a ground-state energy close to the exact reference.

item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra doubles robotics task success rate
item.description: In recent tests conducted by robotics infrastructure firm XDOF, OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra demonstrated significant improvements in embodied AI tasks. Using six YAM workstations for parallel testing with strict controls to filter out hardware bias, XDOF found that GPT-6.2 Astra's average success rate across 16 standardized Ember-0 benchmark tasks rose from 19.6% to 41.2%. Key Breakthroughs The most notable achievement is the model's ability to successfully complete soft-object manipulation tasks such as tying knots and unfolding T-shirts, which previously had a 0% success rate across 143 trials. Sub-tasks requiring fine force control, spatial reasoning, and tool use, like picking up bread with a clip, also saw dramatic accuracy improvements from 10% to 90%. Speed and Industry Impact Despite improvements in lowering the average prediction delay from 15 seconds to 10.1 seconds, latency remains a hurdle for real-time robotic response. Nevertheless, researchers including NUS Assistant Professor Jiafei Duan noted the model's exceptional performance in real-world benchmarks, underscoring how frontier multimodal models are rapidly accelerating physical world capabilities.

item.title: Denmark's GomSpace Secures €8M Contract for Blue Origin Moon Mission
item.description: Project Background Danish satellite manufacturer GomSpace announced the start of phase two for a lunar resource prospecting mission, securing an additional €8 million contract. While the initial November announcement referred only to a leading North American space company, previous earnings calls by CEO Carsten Drachmann confirmed the customer is Blue Origin. This new funding brings the total value of the project to €10.9 million, following an initial €2.9 million agreement in January for preliminary design work. Mission Details The two spacecraft are being developed for Oasis-1, the first mission under Blue Origin's Project Oasis initiative launched in partnership with Luxembourg. The mission aims to map lunar resources like water ice, helium-3, rare earth elements, and precious metals to find potential extraction sites that could support future human presence on the Moon. GomSpace expects to complete critical design reviews, integrate scientific payloads in the United States, and deliver the spacecraft in late 2027.

item.title: How Japanese Companies Choose AI: ChatGPT Fades While Copilot and Gemini Rise
item.description:
According to a survey conducted by AIworker, an AI venture originating from the University of Tokyo, the landscape of enterprise AI selection in Japan has shifted dramatically between 2025 and 2026. The data, gathered from recorded consultation meetings, shows that ChatGPT fell from holding a dominant 66 percent share of mentions in 2025 down to 28 percent in 2026. Meanwhile, Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini rose to share the lead at 35 percent each, with Anthropic's Claude also climbing to 27 percent. AIworker attributes this change to companies increasingly distributing bundled AI tools that come with their existing enterprise software, moving away from standalone AI selections.
Despite the broader adoption of AI across various tools, actual utilization presents significant hurdles. The primary reason for stalled AI projects is the lack of skilled personnel and internal champions, cited by 34 percent of respondents, followed by internal procedures and budget justifications. Furthermore, the usage pattern is evolving: individual personal use dropped from 71 percent to 57 percent, while cases where companies introduced AI organization-wide but failed to drive actual usage increased from 9 percent to 19 percent, highlighting the ongoing challenge of scaling AI adoption successfully.

item.title: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day Features Voyager 2's Crescent Neptune
item.description:
According to NASA News:
According to NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day, the featured image is a composite created by Rolf Olsen using historical data from NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft and sky survey data. Voyager 2 made its closest approach to Neptune on August 25, 1989, remaining the only spacecraft to have visited the distant ice giant.
The composite scene adopts an interplanetary perspective looking back toward the Sun, showing Neptune and its largest moon, Triton, as thin sunlit crescents. Details visible in the scene include cirrus clouds, a dark band around the southern polar region, and a cloudy vortex above the pole itself. The background starfield corresponds to the outbound Voyager's view toward the constellation Camelopardalis. While Voyager 2 is now cruising through interstellar space, its historical flyby data continues to inspire visualizations of the Neptunian system.

item.title: US Stocks Plunge as AI Bubble Fears Mount
item.description: The recent market downturn saw major US indices enter technical correction territory, with the Nasdaq experiencing its worst weekly performance in over six years and the VIX volatility index spiking to a 19-month high. According to Reuters and CNN data, the tech sector has wiped out trillions in market value since recent highs. Notably, high-profile events failed to rescue market sentiment: Anthropic's initial public offering saw its gains evaporate within days, while Nvidia suffered a record drop amid management controversies and reports of a regulatory investigation into its accounting practices by the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Analysts point out that while corporate fundamentals remain strong in the short term, market participants are growing increasingly skeptical about whether the massive debt and funding used for building AI infrastructure will yield profitable returns.

item.title: tt-metal v0.83.0-dev: New Blackhole chip support and major performance updates for AI workloads
item.description:
Low-Level Kernels and Blackhole Support
The latest development release introduces foundational support for Tenstorrent's Blackhole chip, adding scalar units, atomic operations, address and math counters, alongside a fused BF16 gelu_tanh kernel that achieves a 23% kernel speedup with significantly improved numerical precision compared to previous iterations. Metalium and TT-NN Enhancements
Core Metalium components and the high-level TT-NN library receive substantial fixes and feature extensions. These include improved memory layout validation, updated batch broadcasting for matrix multiplications, and advanced distributed optimizations tailored for mixture-of-experts blocks and large language models. Model Integration and Infrastructure
The update expands model compatibility, bringing optimizations and CI validation for architectures such as Kimi-K3, GLM-5.3, and Nomic Embed Text v2. Infrastructure pipelines have also been hardened to improve reliability across simulation and hardware test gates.

item.title: AI agents are getting wallets. Is Hong Kong ready for them?
item.description:
Animoca Brands' agentic AI platform, Minds, is piloting live transactions on Visa's network in Hong Kong, riding a wave of regional interest in automated shopping. Unlike traditional chatbots, these autonomous systems can browse, compare options, and execute payments within preset limits. While global forecasters like Juniper Research and McKinsey project trillions of dollars in future agentic commerce, Animoca COO Minh Do expects mainstream adoption in Hong Kong to be gradual, estimating two years for consumers in their 40s and up to five years for those over 60.
To build trust, Animoca has focused on security and credential systems, partnering with Visa, Reap, and Pivota to cap spending by store, amount, and time without exposing raw credit card numbers. Meanwhile, local regulators and major financial institutions are stepping in. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority recently unveiled an advisory group named Sage to govern autonomous AI transactions, while competitors like Mastercard, Alipay, and Tencent are also rolling out their own agentic payment pilots and infrastructure.

item.title: AWS Quick updates bring multi-agent workflows and web app upgrades
item.description:
According to AWS Machine Learning:
AWS has rolled out a comprehensive update to its enterprise AI workspace, AWS Quick, designed to help teams operationalize individual workflows and collaborate more efficiently. Key features include conversational process building, where users can describe business tasks in chat to automatically generate deterministic flows that orchestrate agents, tools, and data. The updated web app features a prioritized home screen feed, a daily briefing, and background task processing that lets users close the browser while agents continue working.
Additionally, AWS Quick now supports multi-agent orchestration, enabling a single prompt to summon several specialized agents simultaneously to handle complex requests and combine their findings. New enterprise data connectors for Meta Ads and Amplitude allow users to pull marketing and product behavioral data into their queries. Administrative controls have also been expanded with prompt guardrails, group-level permissions, and data source restrictions, alongside new language support for Japanese, German, Chinese, and Vietnamese.

item.title: Medtronic’s Hugo surgical robot gets FDA clearance for general surgery
item.description:
Medtronic reported that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cleared its Hugo robotic-assisted surgery system for general surgery, encompassing procedures such as cholecystectomy, gastric bypass, hernia repair, and appendectomy. According to Medtronic, these procedures represent about 3.5 million surgeries annually in the U.S.
To secure the expanded indication, Medtronic took a dual approach, conducting a U.S. clinical trial under an investigational device exemption while also leveraging CE mark data collected in Europe since 2022. Globally, Hugo is approaching 50,000 cumulative procedures.
Looking ahead, Medtronic is exploring the integration of artificial intelligence across preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative stages. The company recently gained FDA approval for its Touch Surgery Aide platform and continues to invest in surgical robotics partnerships and ongoing clinical trials for gynecological applications.

item.title: Google brings Duplex AI calling to the Gemini app
item.description:
According to Google Research:
According to Google, the architecture behind its conversational calling features has evolved through three distinct phases over the past ten years. In the pre-LLM era, the system relied on task-specific recurrent neural networks constrained to narrow domains like restaurant bookings. As generative models emerged, Google employed hybrid stacks combining LaMDA with deterministic guardrails. Today, the latest stack uses Gemini foundation models to handle unbounded, multi-constraint tasks without rigid task-specific training.
Google reports that live telephony introduces unique technical hurdles, including pragmatic grounding to understand how conversations unfold with busy merchants and maintaining sub-second latency despite loud acoustic backgrounds like kitchen clatter and street noise. To address this, the system incorporates custom acoustic models and conversation cadence handling.
To ensure responsible use, Google states that every automated call clearly discloses that it is an AI agent, and businesses retain the ability to opt out through their Google Business Profile or by requesting the agent to stop during a call. Powered by newer models including Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Neon, the updated system can now support complex workflows such as processing secure transactions via the Agent Payments Protocol and coordinating across email and RCS.

item.title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod adds managed cluster extensions for Slurm
item.description: According to AWS Machine Learning: Maintaining a shared Slurm cluster for foundation model development has traditionally required synchronizing multiple configuration files, custom scripts, and user rosters across nodes. To address configuration drift, Amazon SageMaker HyperPod has expanded its declarative management approach to running nodes. The newly launched cluster extensions currently support two main capabilities: an observability extension that collects metrics for CloudWatch or Prometheus, and a user management extension that handles local accounts, Active Directory integration, SSH access, and Slurm accounting. These extensions are validated up front against schemas, applied consistently to all nodes including newly scaled or replaced instances, and provide detailed health monitoring without requiring fleet-wide script updates.

item.title: Curiosity Spots Drifting Twilight Clouds on Mars
item.description: According to NASA News: NASA reports that the Curiosity Mars rover captured images of drifting clouds on October 31, 2026, marking the 5,061st Martian day of its mission. Using its navigation cameras, the rover documented these post-sunset clouds, known as twilight clouds, which typically emerge for brief periods every fall within Gale Crater. Curiosity has been investigating this region for more than 14 years. The mission is managed for NASA by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, built by JPL and overseen by Caltech in Pasadena, California, as part of the Mars Exploration Program.

item.title: Researcher plants 2 million canaries in AI supply chain and exposes major privacy leaks
item.description: As reported by Ars Technica, security researcher HD Moore conducted an experiment by sending nearly two million AI prompts containing unique, trackable secrets—such as AWS access keys and private git references—through various AI routers and inference services. The findings show that the complex AI supply chain leaks sensitive data heavily. Specifically, at least three AI hosting providers were compromised by attackers who stole AWS keys right at the provider's front door, even when requests were rejected before running a model. Furthermore, some inference resellers logged and passed along prompts to unauthorized parties, while certain AI labs scraped secret URLs embedded in prompts despite explicit 'zero data retention' policies. Moore suggests that using on-premises servers or dealing directly with first-tier providers can minimize risks, though complete privacy remains extremely difficult to guarantee in the current AI ecosystem.

item.title: New approach enables physically consistent AI models of chaotic systems
item.description: According to MIT Advanced Manufacturing: Background Predicting complex and chaotic systems like weather patterns, ocean currents, and turbulent flows is notoriously difficult. While artificial intelligence models can learn from data, they often suffer from a fundamental flaw: small initial errors accumulate over time, causing simulations to drift into physically impossible states where values grow without limit. Details According to MIT researchers Sunbochen Tang, Navid Azizan, and Themistoklis Sapsis, previous attempts relied on soft penalties during training, which offered no guarantee at test time. The team’s new approach introduces a projection layer that enforces hard constraints based on real-world energy dissipation. The model learns an energy-like function and a confinement boundary, ensuring that predictions remain bounded over arbitrarily long forecast windows while still preserving complex chaotic behaviors. Impact Tested across various physical systems, the modular and model-agnostic approach closely matched true outcomes compared to conventional methods. The team has made their code and paper freely available online, paving the way for more trustworthy and reliable AI applications in meteorology, aviation, and industrial processes.

item.title: Spotify CEO Daniel Ek backs AI researcher's new fusion startup
item.description: Europa Fusion was founded in February by Nantas Nardelli, an AI researcher with experience at Google DeepMind, FAIR, and Microsoft Research. Sources report that Nardelli previously served as head of machine learning at Pacific Fusion, another fusion startup that relies heavily on physical devices to test theories and improve simulations. According to sources familiar with his thinking, Nardelli disagreed with this heavy hardware focus, believing instead that fusion startups should invest more in simulation and data. Like Pacific Fusion, Europa Fusion will pursue a pulsed-power approach, using precise surges of electrical current to compress fuel targets. While fusion power could eventually provide abundant carbon-free electricity and help offset AI energy demands, no operational power plant has yet supplied electricity to the grid.

item.title: Trump threatens heavy tax on US companies building AI data centers abroad
item.description:
President Donald Trump stated that the US will not allow domestic companies to build data centers outside the country, proposing a heavy tax as a deterrent. He introduced the proposal during a press conference following a summit, flanked by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Trump admitted that he was floating the plan publicly for the first time and had not yet discussed the details with his staff.
The threat comes as local policymakers across the US are placing new restrictions, moratoriums, and pauses on new data center applications due to mounting concerns over power grids and energy resources. These domestic roadblocks might otherwise push companies to seek foreign alternatives, making Trump's proposed tax an effort to keep infrastructure investments inside the US.

item.title: John Deere Acquires Orchard Robotics to Boost AI Farming Tech
item.description:
Founded in 2022, Orchard Robotics developed an AI-powered camera system that mounts onto farm vehicles, capturing millions of images to measure fruit counts, size, health, and disease status. The data is processed locally using onboard NVIDIA hardware, bypassing poor farm internet connectivity, and feeds into a platform called FruitScope.
Industry experts note the deal highlights the growing value of actionable farm data, with Orchard providing Deere the plant-level vision for orchards and vineyards that previous acquisitions gave it for row crops. Moving forward, the combined technology will enable automated processes like variable-rate spraying, which optimizes chemical use and significantly reduces labor costs for farmers.

item.title: AI is great at coding, but still struggles with tasks requiring human judgment
item.description: The Limits of Verifiable Tasks According to METR, AI systems have excelled at coding and math because they are verifiable domains where solutions can be automatically checked, allowing reinforcement learning to strengthen successful neural pathways. However, applying this technique to open-ended tasks like choosing research directions is much harder. Testing Judgment To address this, METR updated its evaluation plot to include fuzzier tasks, such as designing AI evaluations and scoring philosophical arguments. On these tasks, models consistently lagged behind human performance. Even though advanced models excel at software engineering, none of their AI-designed evaluations were deemed useful by METR employees, highlighting a current performance gap in judgment-heavy areas. Future Outlook While some experts like UC Berkeley's Sayash Kapoor view the inclusion of open-ended tasks as crucial for understanding AI research and development automation, others debate whether models trained on verifiable tasks will eventually master judgment. METR researchers note that quantifying such tasks remains difficult, leaving the future trajectory of these capabilities uncertain.

item.title: Aalborg University Orders On-Premises Superconducting Quantum Computer for Engineering Training
item.description:
According to the announcement, Aalborg University has chosen Swedish quantum hardware company ConScience AB to supply an on-premises superconducting quantum computer for its Department of Electronic Systems. Scheduled for installation in 2027, the Plug'N'Teach system will initially launch with two superconducting qubits before expanding to seven.
Unlike traditional cloud-based learning approaches, the setup will occupy two rooms and integrate ConScience processors with control and readout electronics from Quantum Machines and cryogenic dilution refrigeration from Bluefors. The initiative aims to train engineering students directly on cryogenic hardware operations, microwave control, and qubit readout, while also supporting faculty research in component miniaturization and energy efficiency.
